title: Punch, Japanese macaque baby അമ്മ ഉപേക്ഷിച്ച കുരങ്ങ് കുഞ്ഞ് snow monkey Facts video #wildlife
description:
Snow monkey എന്നറിയപ്പെടുന്ന Japanese macaque ലോകത്തിലെ ഏറ്റവും intelligentയും emotionally complexയും ആയ monkey species-ൽ ഒന്നാണ്. ഇവ സാധാരണയായി അമ്മയും കുഞ്ഞും തമ്മിലുള്ള വളരെ strong bonding കാണിക്കുന്നവയാണ്.

പക്ഷേ Japan ൽ ജനിച്ച Punch എന്ന baby Japanese macaque-ന്റെ ജീവിതം വ്യത്യസ്തമായിരുന്നു…

ജനിച്ച ഉടൻ തന്നെ Punch-ന്റെ biological mother അവനെ ഉപേക്ഷിച്ചു.
Mother-ന്റെ warmth, protection, emotional comfort ഒന്നും ലഭിക്കാത്ത അവസ്ഥയിൽ, Punch cling ചെയ്തത് ഒരു small soft doll-നെയാണ്.

ആ doll Punch-ന് ഒരു toy അല്ലായിരുന്നു…
അത് അവന്റെ അമ്മയായിരുന്നു.

ഈ വീഡിയോയിൽ നിങ്ങൾ അറിയാൻ പോകുന്നത്:

• Japanese macaque species-ന്റെ full scientific details
• Punch-ന്റെ real emotional story
• എന്തുകൊണ്ടാണ് ചില അമ്മമാർ കുഞ്ഞുങ്ങളെ ഉപേക്ഷിക്കുന്നത്
• Attachment-ന്റെ പിന്നിലെ brain science
• Oxytocin എന്ന “love hormone”-ന്റെ role
• Evolutionary survival instinct എങ്ങനെ work ചെയ്യുന്നു

Punch-ന്റെ story നമ്മെ പഠിപ്പിക്കുന്നത് ഒരു powerful truth ആണ്:

Emotional attachment is not weakness…
It is biology. It is survival.

Wildlife, animal behavior, neuroscience, evolution എന്നിവയിൽ താൽപര്യമുള്ളവർക്ക് ഈ വീഡിയോ must-watch ആണ്.

transcript: mother for some reason within days of giving birth at the Ichikawa City Zoo in Japan, is currently being discussed all over the world. He is now only seven months old. The curious video of the baby monkey that gave birth on July 26, 2025, is probably the most viral video of a creature in the world recently. There is a reason for that. He was left alone without a mother and was not in a group. One of the zookeepers gave him a group of ten long, soft orange-colored yarn-like blankets to sleep on. Visuals of the baby monkey constantly playing with it, passing the time, pulling it around like a friend, and sleeping close together, hugging it as if it were in its mother's lap, quickly spread across social media platforms. Everyone felt a sense of pity for the little monkey, just like they would for a human child. People developed a certain fondness for the game after seeing the heartwarming footage of this baby monkey playing without its mother . As more and more footage emerged of other monkeys harassing and chasing it, zoo authorities began to receive protests and responses from many quarters . Many people experienced similar mental anguish, like intense love for an orphaned human child. The visuals of the monkey running away and clinging to the doll, and then sleeping in the same innocent embrace, melted the hearts of people all over the world. People from many regions brought various types of dolls to the zoo to give them to them. As a result, Ikea's dolls became very popular, and various advertisements featured the doll and Punch. Anyway, according to the latest news from Japan, the monkey cub has now established a close relationship with the adult females of the Japanese macaque group, which has about 60 members. With the footage of them holding him, caressing him, grooming him, and licking his fur, people's anxiety and pain have subsided a little. People are wondering about the lives of Japanese macaques, why they abandon their babies like this, why Punch showed such a great affection for this doll with dead fur, and what will happen to Punch now. Welcome to this video. Japanese macaques are monkeys that have evolved special adaptations to survive in extremely cold areas. They can survive in areas covered in snow for months. Hence the name. They are only found in Japan. After humans, they are the only primates on earth that live in extremely cold areas. They can survive even in minus 20 degrees Celsius. The name for this in Japan is Nihon Saru. Nihon means Japan and Saru means monkey, which means Japanese monkey. Japan does not have many different types of monkeys like ours. There is only one species of monkey, the Japanese macaque. Therefore, when they say just Saru or monkey, they mean this one monkey. The macaques that we commonly see in our country are called Bonnet Macaque, Macaca radiata, Lion-tailed Macaque, and Macaca silenus. This monkey belongs to the genus Macaca fuscata. Its scientific name is Macaca fuscata, which means that they are closely related to our monkeys, but they separated from the ancestral monkeys of the Asian macaques about 500,000 years ago. They have evolved with adaptations to survive the cold. Japanese macaques have been studied for a long time by the scientific community for their ability to survive the cold, their habit of bathing in hot springs, and various intelligent behaviors and social habits. The thick fur covering their entire body, the insulation of their oily skin, their habit of sitting close together and touching each other, and their behavior of not being too active, not jumping around too much, and conserving energy through cold behavior. These are the ones that protect themselves from the cold, even though they are important. They exhibit sexual dimorphism. This means that there will be obvious differences in shape and size between males and females . The male will always be larger. Male monkeys weigh between 10 and 14 kilograms . Female monkeys are only half that size. Although there may be coffee-gray hair all over the body, there is no hair on the face. The thin blood vessels, capillaries, that flow through the top layer of the skin on the face are visible as the blood-red milk that flows through them, giving the face a reddish-pink color. They have a very short to 12 cm long bushy tail. They walk on all fours and are semi-terrestrial, meaning they live on the ground and in trees. While males spend more time on the ground searching for prey, females spend more time on trees. They are good swimmers who can jump long distances and can swim up to half a kilometer in a single stretch. They have a longer lifespan than other macaques in this genus, meaning they have a longer lifespan than our monkeys. Males have been seen to live for 32 years and females for 28 years in these Japanese monkeys. They have very complex social relationships and strict hierarchy. They live in large groups of 20 to 100 members, although there may be a dominant male. The group follows a matrilineal system of authority, meaning that the status of a monkey in a group is determined by the status of its mother. Matrilineal rank inheritance, which means that a daughter will receive the rank immediately below her mother's rank, but younger children will have priority, meaning that the lowest girl will have a higher rank than the oldest girl. In a group, there will be more than one maternal uncle and the males belonging to it. If there is no mother, its position will be at the bottom of the group. That is what happened to Panchin. He has no mother's protection and no status in the group. Because he does not have a mother, he has difficulty learning the rules of the group. Since he spent his first months with humans, he also lacked the ability to recognize the body language of macaques. Females stay in the same group for their entire lives. When the males grow up, they leave the group, can mate with other groups, and sometimes return to the old group. This means that this is a matrilineal society, meaning that the female authority and female aunts determine the members of its group with higher status. Males who have been in a relationship with a female for a long time will also gradually increase in status. The power positions in the male group will be in descending order for an alpha male. If the alpha male leaves the group or dies, the person immediately below him will become the alpha male. Even if the group splits into two, a new alpha male will take over. The hierarchy of male monkeys is determined by how long they have been with the group. The main thing that female monkeys do constantly to maintain and develop closeness and love with other group members is to run their fingers through the fur and caress it. This is also the body cleaning of other monkeys. Picking off dirt, fleas, and lice from the fur and a caress with it will help a lot with emotional attachment. This is a kind of huddling. We humans also have this habit of hugging. The intense closeness that individuals create between themselves, such as hugging and shaking hands, is part of it. All this is a play on the love hormone oxytocin. This kind of grooming behavior is not always shown by females to all females. Although stroking the fur of males is important to remove dirt and to maintain and increase emotional closeness with the dominant male in the group. Mothers will pass this caressing training on to their babies. Children acquire this social culture by seeing and experiencing what their mothers do in groups. It is not only genetic, but Punch did not get any of this. Meanwhile, a few days ago, a video of an adult monkey in a new group dragging Punch caused great fear among people and caused a big protest. In fact, it was not a physical harm. It was a kind of social punishment. Since Punch did not behave properly with another baby monkey, the punishment for it was not a fatal harm in a way that would cause injury. This is very common in such monkeys, according to the zoo. Officials had to explain that their courtship period lasts for 16 days, during which they forage, rest, travel, and mate together, and they can form an intense emotional bond. During the mating season, a female will mate with an average of four males. Higher- ranking males get more time and more opportunities to mate. Higher- ranking males sometimes interfere with mating, but the female will approach any male to mate. During mating, the male's face and penis turn red, and the female's face, genitals, and back glow scarlet red. The gestation period is 173 days. When it is time to give birth, the mother will find a safe place away from the group. The baby spends the first month snuggled in her mother's belly, feeding only on breast milk. The babies have dark coffee-colored fur. By five or six weeks, the babies will start eating solid food, and then they will be clinging to their mother's back. This movement, clinging to the fur, is what gives the babies their muscles. The baby did not get that opportunity, so they gave him a long, stringy doll that could be held tightly. Usually, the mother monkey will raise the baby until the age of one. There will be an intense bond between the mother and the baby. The mother will teach the baby many things. Then the mother will slowly return to the old group life. However, sometimes, females who do not have babies will also care for the babies of other monkeys, and the older males in some groups will also care for and protect the babies. By three to four months, the babies will grow to the point where they can jump and run well. At seven months, the mother will wean them and discourage them. After one year, they will stop completely. It has been noted that these species exhibit higher intelligence than other macaque monkeys. In 1950, when a group of Japanese macaque monkeys on Poshima Island were given sweet potatoes Researchers noticed some things. When these sweet potatoes were placed in the soil, they were observed to rub their fur or other objects to remove soil and dust. Then they eat it. But that day, one of the monkeys in the group threw this sweet potato into the water. So he washed the dirt off and ate it. The other monkeys were noticing this amazing thing. Later, I slowly noticed that other monkeys were also continuing the same habit. I noticed that these types of sweet potatoes, which were covered in dirt, were being washed in seawater . Not only did they all learn and follow it, but other groups who saw it also learned it. All but the very oldest monkeys in the group were later observed to continue this habit. This means that such learning develops as part of their culture . Similarly, they learn various fun habits like rolling snowballs in the snow, enjoying themselves in groups in hot springs, and bathing in hot springs. It is understood that they learn various fun habits like humans and transmit these habits from group to group. As a result, they are widely used in neurological scientific research and medicine research. These are mixed monkeys. They eat leaves, flowers, honey, fruits, seeds, skin, roots, tubers, and soil of various plants. In addition to insects, they eat young animals, mushrooms, and fish. The loss to agriculture due to these monkeys in 2019 is estimated to be 900 million yen. Then, every year, about 20 Japanese macaques are killed by culling. However, such culling has greatly reduced their number, but they are still included in the Least Concern category. Let's come to Punch. Why did Punch's mother abandon him? In fact, this kind of maternal rejection is common in many animals. This is common among our elephants. At the time of birth, Panch's mother was only four years old. It was her first birth. She was a first-time mother. This could have been due to some emotional turmoil that caused Panch to abandon her. In addition to this, the stress caused by the severe heat waves at that time could also be a reason. Apart from this, lack of breast milk, significant health problems for the baby, serious diseases, and other conditions like these. If there are any such conditions, the law of nature is to leave those with less survival potential to die. It is not beneficial to raise it or to set aside time and resources for it. If it is seen that it is ultimately an obstacle to the mother's survival or the opportunity to have the next better baby, it is a loss. If this is understood, this practicality will take precedence over motherhood. Surely many animals will abandon their babies like this. That is what happens naturally in nature. There are many reasons why they gave Panch a baby without a mother. If it doesn't get used to holding on tightly, the muscles in its arms won't gain their natural strength. Additionally, if a child does not receive a sense of emotional security, it will also affect their brain development. The sense of security and comfort we feel when we hug the baby doll we received as a replacement is very important. Its resemblance to a monkey in appearance and long, grasping limbs may have helped it be considered a surrogate mother . It has been proven in experiments conducted long ago that baby monkeys prioritize this comfort and security over food . There are some very famous experiments conducted on rhesus monkeys by American psychologist Harry Harlow in the 1950s. He took many baby monkeys away from their mothers, raised them in isolation, and conducted many experiments and observations. One of them is very famous. A puppet monkey made of metal wires and pieces of wood and a puppet monkey covered in dead cloth would be placed in the cage. The puppet made of metal wires would be accompanied by a milk bottle. He conducted various experiments with and without the milk bottle. As soon as the puppet drank milk from the puppet made of world wires, the baby monkey would run to the puppet made of dead cloth and stick to it. This means that this monkey always went to the monkey wrapped in metal only for food. This means that for the baby monkey, the comfort provided by the puppet made of cloth that provided warmth and softness was more important than milk or food. Along with this, he also conducted some experiments. When a doll with a frightening appearance and a distorted face was brought near it, the frightened baby monkey would immediately run towards it and stick to it. It was observed that it had gained a special sense of security and courage. Gradually, it stopped showing fear and sometimes even started showing courage to the terrifying doll. It also lay down comfortably and slept, not realizing that the comfort of the cloth gave the baby monkey an interest beyond food. Scientists had previously thought that babies show special interest in their mothers because they showed love by feeding them and breastfeeding them. However, this study has shown that safety, love, and care are more important for emotional and mental development than food. This has shown that the same thing happens in humans. This also means that physical touch, the sense of security it provides, is what children do without their mothers. These findings have helped in detailed further studies, such as the one that could cause problems. However, for such experiments, this child monkey faced great criticism for being so cruel to him. One of the reasons why animal rights organizations in the world quickly grew and flourished was the opposition to this experiment. In the case of Punch, the love he showed for that doll is an evolutionary survival strategy. There is nothing unnatural about it. When a baby is born, the survival circuits in its brain are already in action. When fear comes, the amygdala in our brain is stimulated. It produces cortisol, which is a stress hormone, which is dangerous. On the other hand, when it receives its mother's touch, the hormone oxytocin is released. This reduces stress and calms the brain. Punch Punch does not have a mother to give him such touches. That soft, gentle touch calmed his brain. This is true for all of us. When we are scared or worried, a touch from someone else, a caress, a hug, is so valuable. It can provide comfort that nothing else can. Whatever it is, now they are The time given to the puppet is being reduced and the time given to it to interact with other monkeys is being increased, and so is the time now when it spends more time with the adult monkeys. The adult female monkeys have started grooming it. They will slowly become part of the group. After a while, the puppet will be abandoned. That's it.
